items.name: Condado Beach
items.hours: Sunrise to sunset (24 hrs accessible; lifeguards 8am-5pm)
items.description: Sheltered urban beach flanked by hotels and restaurants, with calm turquoise water ideal for swimming. The wide sidewalk promenade is perfect for a sunset stroll after a dip.
items.why_it_matters: The quintessential SJ beach — zero travel time from Condado hotels and walkable from Old San Juan via rideshare.
items.walkability_from_old_san_juan: 10 min Uber / 25 min walk along Ashford Ave

items.name: Playa de Isla Verde
items.description: Wide, palm-lined Atlantic beach with stronger surf than Condado, set against a skyline of resort hotels. Vendors rent chairs and water-sports equipment on weekends.
items.why_it_matters: One of Puerto Rico's best urban beaches for people-watching, parasailing, and active beach culture without leaving the metro.
items.gear_needed: Swimsuit + reef-safe sunscreen + towel; cash for chair rental

items.name: Ocean Park Beach
items.description: Laid-back residential beach beloved by locals, kite-surfers, and yoga practitioners. Calmer crowds than Isla Verde with soft white sand and reliable trade winds.
items.why_it_matters: The local's alternative — minimal tourist crowds and the best kite-surfing conditions of any San Juan beach.
items.gear_needed: Swimsuit + reef-safe sunscreen; binoculars optional for bird-watching

items.name: Piñones Beach & Kiosk Strip (Playa Los Bohíos)
items.hours: Beach: sunrise to sunset. Kiosks: Fri-Sun 10am-8pm (busiest Sat-Sun)
items.description: A string of wild Atlantic beaches backed by a mangrove lagoon and a legendary row of frituras kiosks. Rent a bicycle on the paved coastal path that winds through the reserve.
items.why_it_matters: The most authentic Puerto Rican beach-day experience near SJ — local food, scenery, and a free bike-path rarely on tourist itineraries.
items.gear_needed: Swimsuit + reef-safe sunscreen; cash for kiosks and bike rental (~$10/hr)

items.name: Reserva Natural de Piñones Kayak & Mangrove Tour
items.hours: Tours typically 9am-12pm and 2pm-5pm; advance booking required
items.description: Paddle through a protected mangrove lagoon just east of San Juan with a local naturalist guide who explains the ecosystem, birds, and marine life hiding under the roots.
items.why_it_matters: Closest rainforest-like paddling to San Juan — a calm, photogenic alternative to the bio bay for daytime wildlife seekers.
items.gear_needed: Clothes you don't mind getting wet + water shoes + reef-safe sunscreen; paddle gear provided

items.name: La Mina Falls — El Yunque Rainforest
items.hours: El Yunque NF open 7:30am-5:30pm daily; timed-entry passes required in advance
items.description: The most popular El Yunque hike: a 1.8-mile round-trip trail (Angelito + La Mina trails) through tropical forest ending at a 35-ft waterfall with a natural swimming pool. Trail reopened 2022 post-Maria.
items.why_it_matters: Bucket-list Puerto Rico experience — swimming under a rainforest waterfall is the defining 'I was here' moment for most visitors.
items.walkability_from_old_san_juan: 45 min drive SE via PR-3 / PR-191 (Palo Colorado Visitor Center entrance)
items.gear_needed: Hiking sandals or water shoes + swimsuit + insect repellent + water; timed-entry pass (~$2) from recreation.gov

items.name: Yokahú Tower & Big Tree Trail — El Yunque
items.hours: El Yunque NF: 7:30am-5:30pm; timed-entry required (same day-use pass as La Mina)
items.description: A 1.2-mile paved interpretive loop (Big Tree Trail) through tabonuco old-growth forest leads to the Yokahú stone tower with 360° views of El Yunque's canopy and the Atlantic coast. Reopened post-Maria.
items.why_it_matters: The most accessible panoramic viewpoint in the rainforest — moderate incline, paved surface, and no swimming crowds.
items.walkability_from_old_san_juan: 45 min drive SE (same El Yunque NF entrance; Rte 191 El Portal area)
items.gear_needed: Comfortable walking shoes + water + insect repellent + camera

items.name: El Toro Trail — El Yunque (Summit Hike)
items.hours: El Yunque NF: 7:30am-5:30pm; return before 3pm recommended (afternoon rain). Note: confirm open status at fs.usda.gov before visiting — intermittently closed for restoration.
items.description: The only trail reaching El Toro (3,524 ft), Puerto Rico's highest peak. 8.4-mile round-trip through four distinct forest zones including sierra palm and dwarf cloud forest. Strenuous and remote.
items.why_it_matters: The only summit experience in the Caribbean National Forest — for serious hikers who want solitude and a cloud-forest ecosystem unavailable anywhere else on the island.
items.walkability_from_old_san_juan: 55 min drive SE (Trailhead off Rte 186 near Mameyes, Río Grande — separate from Palo Colorado entrance)
items.gear_needed: Hiking boots (waterproof) + trekking poles + 2L water + snacks + rain jacket + insect repellent + charged phone

items.name: Laguna Grande Bioluminescent Bay Kayak Tour — Fajardo
items.hours: Tours nightly 6pm-10:30pm; new-moon windows brightest. Advance booking essential — popular tours sell out weeks ahead.
items.description: Paddle a clear-bottom kayak through a mangrove channel into Laguna Grande, where single-celled dinoflagellates (Pyrodinium bahamense) make the water glow neon blue with every stroke. One of only a handful of bio bays worldwide.
items.why_it_matters: A once-in-a-lifetime natural phenomenon — the closest bioluminescent bay to San Juan and the most practical for a SJ-based day trip (no ferry or overnight needed).
items.walkability_from_old_san_juan: 1 hr drive E via PR-3 to Las Croabas, Fajardo
items.gear_needed: Dark clothing (avoid white — it glows and distracts), water shoes, bug spray, dry bag for phone; kayak + guide provided

items.name: Snorkeling at Las Croabas & Seven Seas Beach — Fajardo
items.hours: Seven Seas open daily sunrise to sunset; boat snorkel charters depart 9am-1pm
items.description: Seven Seas is a calm, crescent-shaped beach in a protected bay. Snorkel from shore over healthy coral, or join a half-day boat charter to the cays of La Cordillera for pristine reef and sea turtles.
items.why_it_matters: The best reef snorkeling reachable as a day trip from SJ without catching a ferry — calm, clear water and regular sea turtle sightings.
items.walkability_from_old_san_juan: 1 hr drive E via PR-3 to Fajardo
items.gear_needed: Swimsuit + reef-safe sunscreen + reef-safe snorkel mask (or rent on-site); water shoes recommended

items.name: El Morro Fort Ramparts & Sunset Walk — Old San Juan
items.hours: NPS: 9am-6pm daily. The esplanade (exterior lawn) is open sunrise to sunset — free access. Interior fort: $10 adult / $5 child.
items.description: The grassy esplanade stretching from La Perla to El Morro is where locals fly kites at sunset with the 16th-century fortress as backdrop. The rampart walls offer Atlantic panoramas and crashing surf views.
items.why_it_matters: The single most iconic free outdoor experience in Puerto Rico — equal parts history, architecture, and jaw-dropping Atlantic scenery.
items.walkability_from_old_san_juan: Walkable — 15 min on foot from Plaza de Armas
items.gear_needed: Comfortable walking shoes; camera for golden hour

items.name: Surfing & Surf-Watching at La Punta (Pine Grove) — Isla Verde
items.hours: Beach access sunrise to sunset; surf conditions best Oct-Mar (NE swells)
items.description: Pine Grove is Isla Verde's reef break, beloved by intermediate surfers. Non-surfers can watch from the rocky point or book a lesson with a local surf school operating from the beach.
items.why_it_matters: The closest consistent surf spot to central SJ — great for watching skilled local surfers or booking your first lesson without a long drive.
items.gear_needed: Swimsuit + reef-safe sunscreen; surf lesson rental includes board + rash guard (~$60/2 hrs with instructor)

items.name: Luquillo Beach (Balneario La Monserrate) — Luquillo
items.description: A crescent mile of calm, coconut palm-shaded beach with the green Sierra de Luquillo mountains as backdrop. The adjacent kiosk row (El Kioskos) serves Puerto Rico's best alcapurrias, bacalaítos, and cold Medalla.
items.why_it_matters: The postcard Puerto Rico beach — where locals from across the island come for a perfect combination of calm water, mountain backdrop, and legendary beach food.
items.walkability_from_old_san_juan: 40 min drive E via PR-3 (Luquillo exit)
items.gear_needed: Swimsuit + reef-safe sunscreen + towel; cash for kiosks (~$3-8/item) and parking ($4/car)

items.name: Kayaking Río Espíritu Santo — Río Grande (El Yunque foothills)
items.hours: Tours depart 9am and 2pm daily; advance booking required
items.description: Paddle the Espíritu Santo River, one of Puerto Rico's cleanest rivers, through a corridor of bamboo and tropical trees at the base of El Yunque. Calm flat-water suitable for beginners; passes through protected forest reserve land.
items.why_it_matters: A serene river-in-the-rainforest experience that pairs perfectly with an El Yunque hike — totally different ecosystem than the coastal activities and rarely crowded.
items.walkability_from_old_san_juan: 40 min drive E via PR-3 (Río Grande area)
items.gear_needed: Clothes you don't mind getting wet + water shoes + insect repellent; paddle gear and PFD provided

items.name: Cueva del Indio — Arecibo (Coastal Sea Cave & Taíno Petroglyphs)
items.type: Outdoor coastal hike + sea caves + archaeological site
items.hours: Daily 9am-5pm; small entrance fee collected by local landowners on-site
items.description: Walk across rugged ironshore limestone along the north coast to sea caves carved by Atlantic surf, where pre-Columbian Taíno petroglyphs are carved into the rock. Dramatic blowhole and wave-crash views.
items.why_it_matters: An off-the-beaten-path gem combining archaeology, dramatic coastal geology, and raw Atlantic power — no tour buses, entirely managed by the local community.
items.walkability_from_old_san_juan: 75 min drive W via PR-22 to Arecibo (Rte 681 north coast)
items.gear_needed: Closed-toe shoes (coral rock is sharp) + water + hat + sunscreen; no railings — caution near cliff edges
